sanskrit: nir ito haritasrajam indro vartayate ratham | tenāpi lihna īyate nipiṃṣann ahināmnaḥ ||
english: From here Indra wheels forth the chariot garlanded with green; upon it he rides, licking as he crushes the brood of the serpent.

sanskrit: yenendra dasyūn amṛṇor yena vṛtraṃ parābhinaḥ | tenā śatakrato tvam aher jātāni jambhaya ||
english: With that whereby thou, O Indra, didst smite the Dasyus, with that whereby thou didst crush Vṛtra — with that, O Śatakratu, do thou devour the offspring of the serpent.

sanskrit: praty amodata pṛthivī prati dyauḥ prati sūryaḥ | paidvo yad aśvamātā krandenāhīn apāvapat ||
english: The earth exulted in response, heaven responded, the sun responded, when Paidva, the horse-born one, with his cry swept away the serpents.

sanskrit: yadā paidvo 'śvamātā krandenāhīn apāvapat | rajjū ṣma datvatīḥ śere pūyantīḥ pṛthivīm anu ||
english: When Paidva, the horse-born one, swept away the serpents with his cry, they lay along the earth like ropes with their fangs bitten off, festering.

sanskrit: nāpo jīryanti nāmṛtaṃ nendrāṇī vidhavābhavat | na tvām āstegiṣad viṣam aśmānam iva sāyakam ||
english: The waters do not decay, nor does immortality wane, nor did Indrāṇī become a widow — let the poison not cleave to thee, as an arrow to a stone.

sanskrit: indrāgnī mitrāvaruṇā tvaṣṭāram aditiṃ bhagam | huve 'ham arvantaṃ paidvaṃ mā me 'yaṃ puruṣo riṣat ||
english: Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, Aditi, and Bhaga — I invoke the swift Paidva: may this man of mine come to no harm.

sanskrit: sadyo jāto 'kanikradat solbo vy adhūnuta | krandenāśvasya vājino 'hanyantāhayaḥ pṛthak ||
english: Born straightway, he neighed and shook off the caul; by the cry of the victorious horse the serpents were slain one by one.

sanskrit: imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedase ratham iva saṃ mahemā manīṣayā | bhadrā hi naḥ pramatir asya saṃ sady agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ||
english: This hymn of praise to the worthy Jātavedas we fashion together with devotion, as a chariot; for his guidance over us is auspicious. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: yasmai tvam āyajase sa sādhaty anarvā kṣeti dadhate suvīryam | sa tūtāva nainam aśnoty aṃhatir agne (…) ||
english: He for whom thou dost procure by sacrifice prospers; unhindered he dwells, acquiring excellent manly strength; he hastens onward — no affliction reaches him. O Agni…

sanskrit: bharāmedhmaṃ kṛṇavāmā havīṃṣi te citayantaḥ parvaṇā parvaṇā vayam | jīvātave prataraṃ sādhayā dhiyo 'gne (…) ||
english: We bring fuel; we prepare oblations for thee, attending upon thee season by season. O Agni, guide our thoughts further along the way of living…

sanskrit: śakema tvā samidhaṃ sādhayā dhiyas tve devā havir adanty āhutam | tvam ādityām̐ ā vaha tān hy ūṣmasy agne (…) ||
english: May we be able to kindle thee; may we direct our thoughts aright — in thee the gods eat the oblation poured out. Do thou bring hither the Ādityas, for thou art their heat, O Agni…

sanskrit: tvam adhvaryur uta hotāsi pūrvyaḥ praśāstā potā januṣā purohitaḥ | viśvā vidvām̐ ārtvijyā dhīra puṣyasy agne (…) ||
english: Thou art the Adhvaryu and the ancient Hotṛ; the Praśāstṛ, the Potṛ; by birth the Purohita. Wise one, knowing all priestly offices, thou dost fulfill them, O Agni…

sanskrit: diśāṃ gopā asya caranti jantavo dvipāc ca yad uta catuṣpad aktubhiḥ | citraḥ praketa uṣaso mahām̐ asy agne (…) ||
english: As guardian of the quarters the creatures move about — both the bipeds and the quadrupeds — through the nights. Thou art the brilliant intelligence of the Dawn, the great one, O Agni…

sanskrit: yo viśvataḥ supratīkaḥ sadṛṅṅ asi dūre cit san taḍid ivāti rocase | rātryāś cid andho ati deva paśyasy agne (…) ||
english: Thou who art of fair aspect on all sides and of like appearance, even when far away thou blazest forth like lightning. Even through the darkness of night dost thou see, O divine Agni…

sanskrit: pūrvo devā bhavatu sunvato ratho 'smākaṃ śaṃso abhy astu dūḍhyaḥ | tad ā jānītota puṣyatā vāco 'gne (…) ||
english: May the chariot of the one who presses soma be foremost among the gods; may our praise be hard to overcome. Know this, and cherish our words, O Agni…

sanskrit: vadhair duḥśaṃsām̐ apa dūḍhyo jahi dūre vā ye anti vā ke cid atriṇaḥ | athā yajñāya gṛṇate sugaṃ kṛdhy agne (…) ||
english: With thy weapons smite away those of evil speech, hard to overcome; whosoever are devourers, whether far or near. Then make an easy path for the sacrificer who sings thy praise, O Agni…

sanskrit: yad ayukthā aruṣā rohitā rathe vātajūtā vṛṣabhasyeva te ravaḥ | ād invasi vanino dhūmaketunā- -agne (…) ||
english: When thou dost yoke the ruddy red steeds to thy chariot, wind-driven — thy roar is like that of a bull; then thou dost impel the forests with thy smoke-banner, O Agni…

sanskrit: adha svanād uta bibhyuḥ patatriṇo drapsā yat te yavasādo vy asthiran | sugaṃ tat te tāvakebhyo rathebhyo 'gne (…) ||
english: Even birds were afraid at thy roar, when thy sparks that feed on grass scattered abroad. Let there be an easy road for thy chariots, O Agni…

sanskrit: tvaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya dhāsy avayātāṃ marutāṃ heḍo adbhutaḥ | mṛḍā su no bhūtv eṣāṃ manaḥ punar agne (…) ||
english: Thou dost sustain the will of Mitra and Varuṇa; the wrath of the Maruts — wondrous — is turned away. Be gracious to us; may their mind return in favor, O Agni…

sanskrit: devo devānām asi mitro adbhuto vasur vasūnām asi cārur adhvare | śarmant syāma tava saprathastame 'gne (…) ||
english: Thou art the divine Mitra of the gods, wondrous; the dear Vasu of the Vasus at the sacrifice. May we dwell in thy most wide-spreading protection, O Agni…

sanskrit: tat te bhadraṃ yat samiddhaḥ sve dame somāhuto jarase mṛḍayattamaḥ | dadhāsi ratnaṃ draviṇaṃ ca dāśuṣe 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ||
english: That is thy good gift: kindled in thine own house, fed with soma, most gracious to old age — thou dost bestow treasure and wealth upon the pious offerer. O Agni, may we never suffer harm in thy friendship.

sanskrit: yasmai tvaṃ sudraviṇo dadāśo 'nāgās tvam adite sarvatātā | yaṃ bhadreṇa śavasā codayāsi prajāvanto rādhasā te syāma ||
english: He to whom thou hast given rich wealth, O giver of goodly goods — sinless thou, O Aditi, in thy wholeness — him whom thou dost urge on with thy auspicious might: may we be possessed of offspring and of thy bounty.

sanskrit: sa tvam agne saubhagatvasya vidvān asmākam āyuḥ pra tireha deva | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Do thou, O Agni, knowing the way of good fortune, extend here the life of us, O divine one. May Mitra and Varuṇa grant us that, and Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven.
